# Called through purego (the Go language's `cgo` option set to "purego"), a
# C function is opened from the library its c.link names, and crosses Go's
# own values: what purego cannot do is refused, naming what it is.

# A package whose c.link ships C to compile: purego has no compiler. gtk4's
# runtime is C until the runtimes become SNGL.
! sngl generate --platform=gtk4 --lang=go --opt cgo=purego -o out window.sngl
stderr 'purego compiles no C, and the package declaring it ships sngl_gtk.c'

# A c.link naming no library: nothing says what to open.
! sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt cgo=purego -o out nolib.sngl
stderr 'cos: purego opens the library a c.link names \(library=…\), and the package declaring it names none'

# A ref C fills: purego hands C no Go address.
! sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt cgo=purego -o out ref.sngl
stderr 'div_into takes q: purego hands C no address to fill'

# A callback: purego's are never given back.
! sngl generate --platform=bubbletea --lang=go --opt cgo=purego -o out callback.sngl
stderr 'sum takes f: purego''s callbacks are never given back'

-- window.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("x")
}
-- nolib.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="math.h", system=true)

#[c.native("cos")]
func cos(x float) float

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("{cos(0.0)}")
}
-- ref.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="stdlib.h", system=true, library="c")

#[c.native("div_into")]
func divide(a int, q ref[int])

func f() int {
    var q = 0
    divide(7, &q)
    return q
}

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("{f()}")
}
-- callback.sngl --
import c "sngl:x/c"
import ui "sngl:ui"

c.link(include="sum.h", system=true, library="sum")

#[c.native("sum")]
func sum(n int, f func(int) int, #[c.context] data c.pointer) int

ui.window(title="t") {
    ui.text("{sum(3, func(i int) => i * 2)}")
}
